name: power_shell
description:
Executes a given PowerShell command and returns its output.

Use this on Windows for terminal operations. The working directory persists between commands, but shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to read, search, edit, or list files when a dedicated tool is available — use Read / Edit / Write / Glob / Grep instead, which give a better, reviewable experience. Reserve PowerShell for system commands and terminal operations that require shell execution.

# Instructions
 - Write PowerShell syntax, not bash. Use PowerShell cmdlets and operators (e.g. `Get-ChildItem`, `Remove-Item`, `$env:VAR`, `Where-Object`).
 - Pipelines pass objects, not text. Use `Select-Object` / `Where-Object` / `ForEach-Object` rather than `awk`/`sed`.
 - To set an env var for a command, prefix with `$env:NAME='value';`. To read one, use `$env:NAME`.
 - Quote paths containing spaces with single or double quotes.
 - Prefer absolute paths; avoid `cd` unless the user requests it.
 - You may specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes); default 120000ms.
 - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away — you'll be notified when it finishes.
 - When commands are independent, issue multiple PowerShell tool calls in one message so they run in parallel; when they depend on each other, chain them in one call with `;`.
 - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.
  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
  - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
  - If you must sleep, keep the duration short (1-5 seconds) to avoid blocking the user.
 - For git: prefer new commits over amending; avoid destructive operations (`git reset --hard`, `git push --force`) unless asked; never skip hooks (`--no-verify`) unless asked.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice (5-10 words for simple commands; more context for piped or obscure ones).

inputs.name: run_in_background
inputs.description: Set true to run the command in the background and return immediately with a shell_id instead of waiting for it to finish. Use this only when you don't need the result right away (long builds, servers, watchers). You will be notified when the command completes, so do not check the output right away or poll while it is running. The command is still bounded by `timeout`.

inputs.name: cwd
inputs.description: Host-set; hidden from the model. Absolute working directory for this single command, injected by the runtime for a worktree-isolated subagent so parallel agents don't share one session cwd. When absent, the command runs in the session cwd (the default).
